$comment: Path-based exemptions for scripts/agnostic-check (issue #274). An entry exempts a FILE or DIRECTORY PREFIX, never a phrase: a dated record keeps its historical text (AGENTS rule 8), and a synthesized test fixture is an input rather than a reference. An optional `names` array narrows the exemption to the private NAMES it declares (#369): only values from `private-targets.json`'s `privateNames` list are valid — a private repo target or an operator path is E-ALLOWLIST-INVALID, because a target is not a name — and the file is still scanned for every other name. An entry whose only finding is an operator path stays FILE-WIDE, because a path shape is not a name (`packages/cli/tests/preview.test.ts` is exactly that case, out of scope of #369). Each entry declares WHY it is exempt and the TRIGGER that removes it; an entry — or a name it declares — that suppresses no reference is reported as W-ALLOWLIST-UNUSED so the registry cannot rot silently (same shape as scripts/link-check/allowlist.json). An entry is EITHER narrowed (`names`) OR explicitly whole-file (`fileWide: true`) — never neither: a whole-file exemption must be declared, so that dropping a narrowing is a loud E-ALLOWLIST-INVALID instead of a silent widening (#372, round 2).

entries.reason: negative assertion: `verify:pack` reads the published --help and FAILS when it names one of these private tools (#254). The file must name the class to prohibit it, and the class it names is exactly these three (measured at #369 on the regex at :154) — `skills-studio`, `prompt-studio` and `AGOS`. The exemption is narrowed to them, so any other private name in this script fails E-AGNOSTIC.
entries.removalTrigger: when `verify:pack` is replaced by this gate (the assertion moves here)

entries.reason: negative assertions: the CLI tests prove that the shipped `skills:export --list` output and the published `--help` surface do NOT name the private projection command (#254). Naming the class is the test, and the class this file asserts against is exactly these three names (measured at #369): `skills-studio` is the negative assertion on `skills:export --list`'s output at :957, and `skills-studio`/`prompt-studio`/`AGOS` form the PRIVATE pattern at :1021 that the `--help` test matches each help text against. The exemption is narrowed to them, so any OTHER private name reintroduced here — a `premerge` citation, a private contract name — fails E-AGNOSTIC; naming one class no longer blinds the file to the rest.
entries.removalTrigger: when the CLI surfaces no longer need a prohibiting assertion (#254 closes the class)

entries.reason: synthesized test input: the absolute path is the INPUT that proves the privacy scanner flags absolute paths — the gate would be untested without a path to detect. OUT OF SCOPE of #369: the finding here is an operatorPath shape (an absolute-path fixture), and `names` can only express `privateNames`, so the entry stays file-wide; a name-scoped exemption is not applicable without inventing a new mechanism.
entries.removalTrigger: when the privacy scanner's absolute-path case is driven from a fixture file instead
